questions.question: Which function allocates a block of uninitialized dynamic memory?
Which function allocates an array-like block and initializes its allocated bytes to zero?
Which function releases memory previously allocated by malloc, calloc, or realloc?
What does realloc generally do?
options: A. Changes the size of an existing allocated block, possibly moving it
B. Always frees memory without allocating
C. Only initializes memory to zero

questions.question: What should a program generally do with a successful dynamic allocation when the memory is no longer needed?
options: A. Call free on the allocated block
B. Call printf on the pointer
C. Call fopen on the pointer

questions.question: What is a memory leak?
options: A. Allocated memory that is no longer reachable or properly released
B. A syntax error in a pointer declaration
C. A compiler warning about integers
D. A file with no newline

questions.question: What is a dangling pointer?
options: A. A pointer that refers to an object whose lifetime has ended or memory that has been released
B. A pointer that always equals NULL
C. A pointer to a valid global variable
D. A pointer to a string literal only

questions.question: What does malloc return on allocation failure?
options: A. A valid pointer to zero bytes

questions.question: Why can realloc be dangerous if used carelessly?
options: A. It may move the allocation, invalidating pointers into the old block
B. It always makes the block smaller
C. It cannot allocate any memory
D. It automatically makes all pointers NULL

questions.question: Which memory area is commonly associated with malloc and related dynamic allocation?
